title: Safe apply + rollback (Optimize config) — working notes / scratchpad
content:
Doc intent: scratchpad for the Safe apply + rollback mechanism for Optimize config. This is not the “official” spec; it’s where we dump evolving decisions + API sketches + edge cases + TODOs. If you need a canonical answer, check Confluence/ADR once those are in review.

Last updated: 2025-03-02 (Dylan)

---

0) Why are we doing this (context reminders)
- We’ve had multiple incidents where an Optimize knob change (batching/quant/cache/routing policy) caused a customer-visible regression, and the mitigation path was “find last good config, manually paste it back, hope it propagates.” Too slow, too error-prone.
- Goal: versioned history + safe apply with preflight + one-click rollback with audit trails and RBAC. Works across Hosted, Dedicated, Private.
- Success is MTTR reduction + lower change-failure rate.

Related motivating ticket(s)
- Jira SUP-2418: “latency regression after optimization config change”
- Slack incidents/thread-1731349988 (notes: manual mitigation, couldn’t confidently identify last known-good)

---

1) Current state (as of today)
- Configs exist as “current” blobs keyed by scope (route/model/customer/cluster-ish depending on environment). No immutable history.
- Apply is effectively “write new blob” + best-effort propagation.
- Console has limited visibility (what changed / who / what did runtime actually take?)

---

2) Definitions (shared language)
- “Optimize config”: structured config consumed by runtime that controls batching/caching/quantization profiles/routing knobs (exact schema evolving).
- “Scope”: the target where config applies. We need to be explicit because it drives version keys, blast radius display, and locking semantics.
  - Proposed scope tuple: {tenant_id, deployment_mode, environment, region, cluster_id?, route_id, model_id}
  - NOTE: for Hosted we likely don’t expose cluster_id; for Dedicated/Private we may.
- “Version”: immutable snapshot of the whole config document + metadata (author, reason, linked ticket, etc). Whole-config rollback (no patch rollback in v1).
- “Apply”: set desired active version for a scope; triggers propagation rollout.
- “Rollback”: same as apply, but operator selects a prior version (known-good) as target.

---

3) Decisions (tentative / in motion)
3.1 Whole-config rollback (not patch)
- Decision direction: Whole-config rollback only for initial release.
- Reason: patch rollback seems attractive but makes it harder to reason about safety and “what is the running config?” esp. when schema changes.
- Exception we keep mentioning: some fields may be runtime-derived or “read-only” (e.g., computed defaults). If these exist, we need to be super clear in diff/preview UI.

3.2 Immutable version store + separate “active pointer”
- Version records are immutable.
- Active version pointer per scope can be updated (with optimistic concurrency).
- We need a notion of “applied_version_id” vs “propagated_version_id” (what runtime is actually at).

3.3 Locking model
- Require a per-scope lease/lock to prevent concurrent apply/rollback.
- Lease should cover the entire rollout duration.
- If lease holder dies: lease expiry + safe takeover.
- Runtime team (Mateo) wants deterministic behavior under split-brain conditions; we should assume partial propagation can happen and must be detectable.

3.4 Audit events are non-negotiable
- Every attempt and outcome: apply_attempted/applied/failed, rollback_attempted/rolled_back/failed.
- Include what/where/who, request_id/idempotency_key, and propagation summary.

---

4) Storage + data model sketches (rough)
NOTE: not committing to DB details here; see ADR once merged.

Entity: optimize_config_version
- version_id (uuid)
- scope_key (string; stable canonical serialization of scope tuple)
- scope fields (tenant_id, env, region, route_id, model_id, …) (denormalize for filtering)
- parent_version_id (nullable; useful to show lineage)
- created_at
- created_by (user_id + display)
- source (console|api|automation|migration)
- reason (free text)
- linked_ticket (e.g., Linear/Jira URL)
- config_schema_version (int/string)
- config_blob (json)
- config_hash (sha256 for dedupe + integrity)

Entity: optimize_config_active
- scope_key
- active_version_id
- updated_at
- updated_by
- update_reason
- optimistic concurrency token (etag / version counter)

Entity: optimize_config_rollout
- rollout_id
- scope_key
- target_version_id
- kind (apply|rollback)
- status (pending|running|succeeded|failed|canceled|timed_out)
- started_at, finished_at
- initiated_by
- idempotency_key
- lease_id
- canary params (if any)
- gate evaluation results (latency/error/etc)
- propagation status summary

We keep going back and forth about whether to keep rollout table separate vs embedding into audit stream. Leaning separate because Console needs a “progress page” with polling.

Backfill plan
- ENG-4821: Backfill current live configs as v0 with source=migration.
- Question: do we create v0 per scope even if config blob identical across scopes? Probably yes for simplicity; allow dedupe by hash but store separate version rows (or store once and reference). TBD.

Retention
- Enterprise asks for longer retention (SUP-2423). Minimum: 90 days? Preferred: 1 year? Private may want configurable.
- Storage cost vs compliance trade-off. We should support TTL by policy + “legal hold” for certain tenants.

---

5) API sketches (control plane)
NOTE: names not final; writing down shape so FE + BE align.

5.1 List versions
GET /v1/optimize/configs/versions?tenant_id=&route_id=&model_id=&region=&limit=&cursor=
Response fields:
- versions[]: version_id, created_at, created_by, reason, linked_ticket, config_schema_version, config_hash
- pagination: next_cursor

5.2 Get a version
GET /v1/optimize/configs/versions/{version_id}
Response:
- version metadata
- config_blob

5.3 Compare versions (server-side diff)
POST /v1/optimize/configs/versions/compare
Body:
- from_version_id
- to_version_id
Response:
- diff_summary (human readable)
- diff_json (structured diff)
- warnings[] (e.g., “quantization profile change may require warmup; expect transient p95 spike”)

Open question: do we want diff_json to be JSON Patch (RFC 6902) vs custom tree diff? FE preference: custom tree diff with paths + old/new + “kind”. Runtime/SRE preference: stable & loggable. Might do both.

5.4 Create a new version (draft)
POST /v1/optimize/configs/versions
Body:
- scope
- config_blob
- reason
- linked_ticket
- validate_only? (bool)
Response:
- version_id
- validation results (if validate_only)

Question: do we allow “create version” separate from “apply”? Product wants a “safe apply wizard” that effectively creates a version as part of applying. But we still need ability to stage versions for later.

5.5 Safe apply (preflight + optional canary)
POST /v1/optimize/configs/apply
Body:
- scope
- version_id (or config_blob to create+apply)
- idempotency_key
- canary: {enabled, percent, duration_minutes}
- gates: {latency_p95_max_delta, error_rate_max, …} (optional overrides)
- require_justification (if policy)
Response:
- rollout_id
- status

5.6 Rollback to a prior version
POST /v1/optimize/configs/rollback
Body:
- scope
- target_version_id
- idempotency_key
- reason
- linked_ticket (required for prod? policy-dependent)
Response:
- rollout_id
- status

5.7 Rollout status
GET /v1/optimize/configs/rollouts/{rollout_id}
Response:
- status
- progress breakdown by region/cluster (careful: cluster details might be privileged)
- gate results
- correlation ids (for logs/metrics)

---

6) Console UX notes (non-polished)
Kenji’s early notes are in product Drive doc; these are just engineering reminders.

6.1 Version history page
- Timeline list sorted newest first.
- Show: author, timestamp, reason, linked ticket, “Applied to: <scope>”, and “Status: active / not active / failed rollout / partially propagated”.
- Need “Copy version ID” because support/SRE will paste into runbooks.
- Must include deep link to audit log entries (and to rollout status page).

6.2 Compare modal
- Show changed fields grouped by category: batching / caching / quantization / routing.
- Provide “risk callouts” from preflight (warnings).
- Must be usable even with large nested configs; include search by key path.

6.3 Safe apply wizard
- Step 1: select scope
- Step 2: edit config (or “import from Optimize recommendation”)
- Step 3: preview diff vs active
- Step 4: run preflight validation (blocking errors + warnings)
- Step 5: choose rollout strategy: immediate vs canary (if enabled)
- Step 6: confirm (show blast radius, required permissions, require ticket)

6.4 Rollback flow
- “Rollback” button present on active version page and also on any historical version.
- Confirmation dialog must show:
  - target version (timestamp, author)
  - what will change (diff summary)
  - blast radius (scope breakdown)
  - whether this triggers cache invalidation / warmup and expected transient impact
  - must capture reason + linked ticket for prod (SRE wants this, security wants this)

Copy note: We should avoid implying “instant” rollback. Better: “Initiate rollback” then show progress + explicit “when complete” criteria.

---

7) Preflight validator rules (rough list)
Owned by ENG-4824 (validator service), but listing here to align.

Hard errors (block apply)
- schema invalid / unknown fields
- batch.max_tokens_per_batch exceeds global max for model family or tier
- quantization profile incompatible with model architecture / weights format
- caching settings conflict (e.g., enable_kv_cache=false but prefix_cache=true)
- routing policy references unknown model IDs / regions

Warnings (allow apply but require acknowledgement)
- large jump in batch size (>2x)
- changing quantization profile while load is high (if we have signal)
- disabling cache likely increases cost; show cost impact estimate if available
- enabling aggressive continuous batching might increase tail latency for interactive routes

Nice-to-have (post v1)
- simulate expected throughput/latency impact using recent traffic histogram
- incorporate quality/evals regression gate for some customers (but this is explicitly not fully automated rollback; still can be a gate that fails apply)

Open question: where do we store validation output so it’s auditable later? (We probably want to persist the validation result object with the rollout record.)

---

8) Canary + metric gates (notes)
- Default gates: p95 latency delta and error rate.
- Need tier-specific thresholds (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).
- Gate evaluation window: at least 10 minutes? But SRE wants rollback within minutes during incident; we may need “fast gate” mode.

Signals we probably can rely on
- p95 latency by route/model/scope
- error rate (5xx) by route/model/scope
- saturation metrics (GPU util, queue depth) if available

Hard parts
- Noise / low traffic routes: can’t gate reliably. Must fall back to “no gate” or broaden scope for metrics.
- Partial propagation: canary may not isolate cleanly if route spans multiple clusters.

Question: do we require gates for prod by policy? Or just strongly encourage? Product stance: optional with sensible defaults. SRE stance: defaults on, allow override with justification.

---

9) Runtime propagation / edge cases (from runtime threads)
Key runtime concerns captured from Slack eng-runtime/thread-1730919920 and follow-ups:
- KV cache interaction:
  - If caching knobs change, old cache entries may be invalid. Need a clean cache invalidation strategy tied to version_id.
  - Proposed: include config_version_id in cache key namespace; on apply/rollback, runtime naturally stops hitting old entries.
- Continuous batching:
  - Changing batching parameters can cause immediate queueing behavior shift.
  - We should consider “warm apply”: gradually ramp batch settings? (Probably out of v1; at least warn.)
- Quantization profile swaps:
  - May require model reload/warmup; transient latency spikes.
  - We need to communicate this in Console + runbooks.

“Split brain” scenarios
- Control plane thinks active_version=V10 but runtime cluster A is still on V9.
- We need:
  - runtime to report applied_version_id
  - Console to show partial propagation
  - rollback should be safe even when partially propagated (it’s just another rollout), but it must not amplify inconsistency

Leases/locks
- Runtime PR-10479 adds locking/lease + status callbacks. We need to ensure BE and runtime agree on lease semantics (who owns the lease? which service writes it?).

---

10) RBAC + security notes
- New permissions: optimize.config.apply, optimize.config.rollback (ENG-4830)
- Expectation: rollback is more restricted than view history.
- For enterprise tenants:
  - require MFA? (separate track)
  - require justification + linked ticket for rollback/apply in prod
- Security wants audit logs immutable and exportable.

Do we need “two-person rule” for rollback? Current stance: no (too slow for incident), but could be a follow-on optional policy for certain tenants.

Internal support (INT-911): SRE on-call role mapping. Need to ensure on-call can rollback in prod without granting broad config edit powers.

---

11) Audit logging (what we think needs to be emitted)
Minimal event set
- optimize_config.apply_attempted
- optimize_config.apply_succeeded
- optimize_config.apply_failed
- optimize_config.rollback_attempted
- optimize_config.rollback_succeeded
- optimize_config.rollback_failed

Fields (must have)
- tenant_id
- scope_key + scope fields
- from_version_id (current active)
- to_version_id (target)
- actor (user/service)
- request_id + idempotency_key
- rollout_id
- timestamps
- result (success/failure)
- failure_reason (if any)

Fields (nice-to-have)
- diff_summary
- validation_summary (errors/warnings)
- gate results summary
- propagation_summary (#targets succeeded/failed)

Redaction notes
- avoid logging full config_blob if it could contain sensitive values (it *shouldn’t*, but be defensive). Prefer hashes + version IDs.

---

12) Release / rollout notes (internal)
Phased rollout plan (mirrors PM-412 notes)
- internal dogfood (single tenant)
- Hosted sandbox
- Hosted prod
- Dedicated
- Private

Feature flags
- flags for version history read
- flags for apply
- flags for rollback
- flags for canary/gates
- flags for audit export (enterprise)

Release readiness checklist (to coordinate with Connor)
- dashboards in place (observability-pack/pr-733)
- incident-bot posts include rollback links (incident-bot/pr-219)
- runbook updated + on-call training session scheduled

---

13) Open questions / unresolved
(Keep this list short + real; if resolved, move to “Decisions” and delete from here.)

Q1: Scope key canonicalization
- How do we guarantee stable scope_key string across services/languages? (Need a canonical serializer.)
- What fields are optional per deployment mode?

Q2: Diff format
- JSON Patch vs custom tree diff; how do we keep it stable across schema versions?

Q3: “Known-good” marking
- Do we allow an operator to mark a version as known-good (tag) after observation? Or do we infer from being active for N hours without incidents?
- SRE wants “fast pick” during incident: “rollback to last known-good.”

Q4: Gate thresholds ownership
- Defaults owned by SRE (Sean/Neha) vs product? Who can override? Where do overrides live (policy engine)?

Q5: Private deployments
- For air-gapped: where do audit logs go? (Local storage + export mechanism?)
- How do we handle migrations/backups for version store? (See private-installer/pr-302)

Q6: Behavior when rollback fails mid-propagation
- If some targets roll back and others don’t, what’s the “active” pointer state? We should not lie.
- Do we allow “force complete” vs “auto retry”? Probably retry with backoff.

---

14) TODO dump (actionable-ish)
- [Felix] confirm version history UI can render huge configs without freezing (virtual list + search)
- [Hannah] ensure rollback confirmation includes blast radius + warmup/caching warning copy
- [Chloe] finalize idempotency behavior on apply/rollback endpoints (what’s returned on retry?)
- [Jada] write down consistent rollout state machine; align with runtime status callbacks
- [Logan] define first-pass gate evaluation implementation details (query window, aggregation)
- [Fiona] review audit fields + retention for enterprise compliance asks
- [Rafael] runbook draft: steps + screenshots placeholders + “partial propagation” troubleshooting

---

Appendix A: Pointers to active engineering work (quick links)
- ENG-4821: schema + migrations + backfill
- ENG-4822: list/get/compare endpoints
- ENG-4823: rollback endpoint (authz + idempotency + audit)
- ENG-4824: preflight validator
- ENG-4825/4826: Console UX
- ENG-4827: runtime atomicity/locking
- ENG-4828: observability + alerts
- ENG-4829: E2E tests
- ENG-4830: RBAC permissions

Appendix B: Incident notes summary (from Slack)
- Pattern: “small config tweak” -> latency spike within minutes -> scramble to revert; team not sure which config was live where.
- Needed: “one button rollback” + “show propagation status” + “tie changes to tickets/owners.”

(End)
